title: Reflections on 40 Years of HIV | David J. Sencer CDC Museum | CDC
content: The David J. Sencer CDC Museum is temporarily closed. Continue to check our website for further updates on when we will reopen. When the museum reopens, all visitors will need to make reservations at least a week in advance. Walk-in visits are no longer permitted. Reflections on 40 Years of HIV Print Minus Related Pages June 5, 2021 marks 40 years since the first official reporting, in CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR) , of five cases describing what later became known as Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) and what is now HIV Stage III. On this 40th anniversary, we remember the more than 32 million people who have died from HIV worldwide since the start of the global epidemic, and the 38 million people currently living with HIV. Along with the global community, we are redoubling our efforts to ensure equitable access to services and prevention strategies, especially for those disproportionately affected by HIV, so that we may end the HIV epidemic in the U.S. and around the world. The CDC Museum invites you to view this collection of representative materials. We Were There Personal experiences of those leading the CDC investigations that shaped health care policy and helped save millions of lives. More External Link Icon Story of CDC: Early AIDS An exhibition exploring CDC’s early response to the HIV epidemic.​ More 40-Year Timeline A 40-year timeline documenting CDCs historic role in addressing the HIV epidemic in the United States and around the world. More EID Journal – June 2021 June 2021 marks the 40th anniversary of the first description of AIDS. More MMWR – June 2021 Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report recognizing this important milestone. More Oral History: Mary Guinan Dr. Guinan remembers the June 1981 MMWR article on Pneumocystis pneumonia and the reaction from the medical community. More Oral History: Ken Castro Dr. Castro describes his first encounters with patients with AIDS and the MMWR article that detailed what he had been seeing. More Oral History: David Auerbach Auerbach talks about his training and the implementation the first national case-control study. More Helene Gayle Gayle explains how she got involved with the HIV/AIDS program at CDC and issues surrounding pediatric/adolescent HIV/AIDS. More Global Health Chronicles A historic collection of oral histories, photographs, documents, and other media representing the early years of AIDS and CDC’s response to the epidemic. More Dr. William Darrow Dr. Darrow delves into his participation on the Los Angeles Cluster Investigation, and how a flight attendant lead became a vector. More Future of Personal Health Dr. Demetre Daskalakis discusses the current state of HIV in the U.S., and the lack of equitable access to HIV prevention and treatment. More Community D.C. Podcast Dr. Daskalakis (CDC) & Harold Phillips (HHS) talk with Jerry Houston about progress that’s been made, PrEP, the importance of HIV testing, a connection to Covid and more.
